audit-p1505.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 46, Pressure Injuries
audit-p1505.auditText: 70 percent of pressure injuries in people over 65; 9 to 22 percent of nursing home residents; 5 to 32 percent of hospital patients.

audit-p1506.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 46, Pressure Injuries
audit-p1506.auditText: healing benchmarks: partial-thickness stage 2 within 60 days maximum, full-thickness stage 3, 4 and unstageable showing improvement every 2 to 4 weeks. Also the pain figures: 87 percent report pain with dressing changes, 84 percent at rest, 42 percent both, 18 percent of those with dressing-change pain report it at the highest level, only 6 percent receive any pain medication.

audit-p1515.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 46, Pressure Injuries
audit-p1515.auditText: the turning trial: 942 nursing home residents on high-density foam, 2.5 percent at two-hourly, 0.6 percent at three-hourly, 3.1 percent at four-hourly, no significant difference. Also the 30-degree side-lying position with the upper leg forward and legs separated by a pillow, and head of bed at the lowest elevation consistent with medical conditions.

audit-p1516.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 46, Pressure Injuries
audit-p1516.auditText: weight shift every 15 minutes where the patient can do it; chair repositioning at least hourly.

audit-p1519.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 46, Pressure Injuries
audit-p1519.auditText: oral nutritional supplements, relative reduction in incidence of 25 percent. Also that serum albumin and prealbumin reflect inflammatory response rather than nutritional status.

audit-p1523.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 46, Pressure Injuries
audit-p1523.auditText: stage 1 reversible but tissues may take 1 to 3 weeks to return to normal; stage 2 heals in 2 to 4 weeks if properly treated; deep tissue injury follows intense pressure about 48 hours prior.

index-c44-060.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 44, Sleep disorders
index-c44-060.auditText: Patients should receive iron supplementation if the serum ferritin is less than 75 mcg/L.

index-c44-061.auditText: Intravenous iron is suggested for those with moderate to severe restless legs syndrome and a ferritin less than 300 mcg/L.

index-c44-063.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 44, Sleep disorders
index-c44-063.auditText: Augmentation is a worsening of restless legs syndrome manifested by earlier onset, increased intensity, or spread of symptoms to the upper extremities and trunk.

index-c44-064.auditText: Augmentation is much more frequent with carbidopa-levodopa than with long-acting dopamine agonists.

index-c44-065.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 44, Sleep disorders
index-c44-065.auditText: Estimates of augmentation on long-acting dopamine agonists range between 2% and 15% per year.

index-c44-068.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 44, Sleep disorders
index-c44-068.auditText: Bupropion is less frequently associated with restless legs syndrome than selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

index-c44-069.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 44, Sleep disorders
index-c44-069.auditText: REM sleep behavior disorder is defined as recurrent complex movements or vocalizations during sleep characterized by dream enactment.

index-c44-072.auditText: Up to 90% of patients who present with REM sleep behavior disorder develop another synucleinopathy disorder over a 10- to 15-year follow-up.

index-c44-078.auditText: Non-REM parasomnias such as sleep walking, confusional arousals, and sleep terrors predominantly occur in the first part of the night.

index-c44-081.auditText: Irregular sleep-wake rhythm disorder is characterized by a lack of a clearly defined circadian rhythm resulting in insomnia at night and excessive sleep during the day.

index-c44-082.auditText: Non-24-hour sleep-wake rhythm disorder usually occurs from a patient's inability to entrain their circadian rhythm to light due to complete blindness.

index-c44-084.auditText: Patients with irregular sleep-wake rhythm disorder will generally sleep for less than 4 hours at a time.

index-c44-110.auditText: In stimulus-control therapy, if the patient cannot fall asleep within approximately 20 minutes they should get out of bed and do a relaxing activity.

index-c47-019.auditText: Acute incontinence refers to those situations where the incontinence is of sudden onset, usually linked to an acute illness or an iatrogenic problem, and subsides once the illness or problem has been resolved.

index-c47-020.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-020.auditText: Persistent incontinence refers to incontinence that is not precipitated by an acute illness and endures over time.

index-c47-021.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-021.auditText: Urine loss among older patients with chronic incontinence with otherwise asymptomatic bacteriuria does not appear to improve with bacteriuria treatment.

index-c47-023.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-023.auditText: The symptoms of stress incontinence are specific and involve leakage coincident with increases in intra-abdominal pressure caused by coughing, sneezing, laughing, or exercising.

index-c47-024.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-024.auditText: Stress incontinence is unusual in men, and it mainly occurs following transurethral interventions for benign prostatic conditions or after surgical or radiation therapy for lower urinary tract malignancy.

index-c47-025.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-025.auditText: Urgency incontinence, when it occurs along with urinary urgency, daytime urinary frequency, and nocturia, has been called wet overactive bladder.

index-c47-026.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-026.auditText: Acute retention of urine is defined as a painful, palpable or percussable bladder, when the patient is unable to pass any urine.

index-c47-027.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-027.auditText: Chronic retention of urine is defined as a non-painful bladder, which remains palpable or percussable after the patient has passed urine.
index-c47-027.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c47-028.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-028.auditText: Functional incontinence results when an older person is unable to reach a toilet on time due to impaired cognitive function and/or mobility.

index-c47-029.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-029.auditText: In acute urinary retention, the distended bladder is a firm, midline mass that emanates from the pelvis and is dull to percussion.

index-c47-030.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-030.auditText: Gross bladder distention of ≥ 500 mL should be easily detected on physical examination.

index-c47-031.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-031.auditText: The sensitivity of the cough stress test is highest when the patient is standing.

index-c47-032.auditText: For the cough stress test, the patient should have a comfortably full bladder at approximately half-capacity of 200 mL.

index-c47-033.auditText: During a cough stress test, delayed leakage after 3 seconds or the initiation of voiding generally indicates a cough-induced bladder contraction.

index-c47-034.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-034.auditText: In nursing home populations, there is no benefit to treating bacteriuria in patients with chronic, stable incontinence.

index-c47-036.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-036.auditText: Postvoid residual values of less than 100 mL in the absence of straining to void generally reflect adequate bladder emptying in geriatric patients.

index-c47-038.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-038.auditText: In women there is evidence that modest weight loss of approximately 5% to 10% of body weight leads to reduction in urinary incontinence episodes.
index-c47-038.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c47-039.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-039.auditText: Pelvic floor muscle exercises are effective in men and women for the treatment of urge, stress, mixed stress-urge incontinence, and incontinence following prostatectomy.

index-c47-040.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-040.auditText: Pelvic floor muscle exercises should be practiced many times throughout the day, building up from 3 seconds to 10 seconds in duration.
index-c47-040.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c47-041.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-041.auditText: Scheduled toileting involves assisting the patient to the toilet at regular intervals, usually every 2 to 3 hours during the day regardless of the presence or absence of the patient's expressed desire to void.

index-c47-042.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-042.auditText: Habit training involves a schedule of toileting that is individually modified according to the patient's pattern of continent voids and incontinence episodes.

index-c47-043.auditText: Prompted voiding involves asking the patient to attempt to void up to three times every 2 hours during the day.

index-c47-044.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-044.auditText: Between 25% and 40% of nursing home residents respond very well to daytime prompted voiding.
index-c47-044.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c47-045.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-045.auditText: Drugs with bladder smooth-muscle relaxant properties used for urgency incontinence are available in two different classes: antimuscarinic and beta-3-agonist.

index-c47-046.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-046.auditText: Most studies suggest a reduction of 60% to 70% in the frequency of incontinence episodes with drug therapy in selected older adults.

index-c47-047.auditText: Multiple epidemiologic studies suggest bladder antimuscarinic drug therapy is associated with a 50% relative increase in the odds of developing dementia.

index-c47-049.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-049.auditText: For older men with overactive bladder symptoms, alpha adrenergic antagonists may be a better choice for first-line drug therapy.
index-c47-049.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c47-051.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-051.auditText: Either opposed or unopposed oral conjugated estrogen therapy has been shown to increase the risk of developing or worsening incontinence.

index-c47-054.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-054.auditText: Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation involves weekly 30-minute stimulation sessions in an outpatient clinical setting for up to 12 weeks.

index-c47-055.auditText: Early trial results suggest that botulinum toxin A therapy lasts 6 months and is equally effective in older and younger age groups.

index-c47-056.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-056.auditText: The goal of intermittent catheterization is to keep residual urine volume generally less than approximately 300 to 400 mL.

index-c47-057.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-057.auditText: The limited evidence available to date does not suggest that routine changing of indwelling bladder catheters is warranted.

index-c47-058.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 47, Incontinence
index-c47-058.auditText: Thirty to fifty percent of older patients in institutional settings with frequent urinary incontinence also have episodes of fecal incontinence.

index-c55-002.auditText: The 2001 WHO International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) characterizes decreases in function as the consequence of a dynamic interaction between various health conditions and contextual factors.

index-c55-003.auditText: The short physical performance battery includes three screening tests: gait speed, timed chair stands, and static balance.

index-c55-009.auditText: To achieve optimal results in increasing muscle strength, the resistance should be 60% to 80% of the person's maximal lifting ability.

index-c55-011.auditText: Exercise programs designed to increase aerobic capacity usually involve continuous activity performed for at least 20 minutes at an intensity that is 50% to 80% of maximal oxygen consumption.

index-c58-010.auditText: The highest prevalence and incidence rates of delirium occur among ventilated intensive care unit patients.

index-c58-011.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-011.auditText: Delirium occurs in up to 48% of patients in nursing homes or postacute settings.
index-c58-011.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-012.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-012.auditText: Delirium occurs in up to 83% of all patients at the end of life.
index-c58-012.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-013.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-013.auditText: Delirium in the intensive care unit is associated with a fourfold increased risk of in-hospital mortality.
index-c58-013.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-014.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-014.auditText: Delirium in the intensive care unit is associated with a sixfold increased risk of mortality at 6 months.
index-c58-014.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-015.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-015.auditText: In the emergency department, delirium is associated with a sevenfold increased risk of mortality at 6 months.
index-c58-015.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-018.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-018.auditText: Removal or treatment of one risk factor alone often fails to resolve delirium.
index-c58-018.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-019.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-019.auditText: Patients with dementia have a two- to fivefold increased risk for delirium.
index-c58-019.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-021.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-021.auditText: In older adults, acute myocardial infarction and congestive heart failure may present with delirium or failure to thrive as the cardinal feature, with minimal symptoms of angina or dyspnea.
index-c58-021.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-022.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-022.auditText: Occult infection is a particularly noteworthy cause of delirium because older patients may not present with leukocytosis or a typical febrile response.
index-c58-022.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-023.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-023.auditText: In 30% or more of delirium cases, use of one or more specific medications contributes to its development.
index-c58-023.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-024.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-024.auditText: Use of any psychoactive medication is associated with a fourfold increased risk of delirium.
index-c58-024.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-025.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-025.auditText: Use of two or more psychoactive medications is associated with a fivefold increased risk of delirium.
index-c58-025.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-026.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-026.auditText: Sedative-hypnotic drugs are associated with a 3- to 12-fold increased risk of delirium.
index-c58-026.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-027.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-027.auditText: Narcotics are associated with a threefold increased risk of delirium.
index-c58-027.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-028.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-028.auditText: Anticholinergic drugs are associated with a 5- to 12-fold increased risk of delirium.
index-c58-028.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-029.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-029.auditText: Fully two-thirds of cases of delirium occur in patients with dementia.
index-c58-029.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-030.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-030.auditText: Mental status changes in delirium typically occur over hours to days, in contrast to dementia which presents insidiously over weeks to months.
index-c58-030.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-031.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-031.auditText: The hypoactive form of delirium is characterized by lethargy and reduced psychomotor functioning and is the more common form in older patients.
index-c58-031.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-032.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-032.auditText: Hypoactive delirium often goes unrecognized and carries an overall poorer prognosis than other forms.
index-c58-032.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-033.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-033.auditText: As few as 20% of patients attain complete delirium symptom resolution at 6-month follow-up.
index-c58-033.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-034.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-034.auditText: Cognitive function is impacted for up to a year following delirium.
index-c58-034.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-035.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-035.auditText: Delirium is a clinical diagnosis relying on bedside observation, cognitive assessment, and history-taking from a knowledgeable informant to establish a change from baseline functioning.
index-c58-035.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-036.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-036.auditText: Inattention can be indicated by an inability to repeat five digits forward.
index-c58-036.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-037.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-037.auditText: Inattention can be indicated by an inability to repeat three digits backward.
index-c58-037.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-038.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-038.auditText: Cerebrospinal fluid examination, brain imaging, and EEG are probably indicated in fewer than 5% to 10% of delirium cases.
index-c58-038.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-039.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-039.auditText: Lumbar puncture with cerebrospinal fluid examination is indicated for the febrile delirious patient when meningitis or encephalitis is suspected.
index-c58-039.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-040.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-040.auditText: Brain imaging should be reserved for delirium cases with new focal neurologic signs, history or signs of head trauma, or without another identifiable cause.
index-c58-040.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-044.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-044.auditText: Implementation of targeted preventive interventions resulted in a 40% risk reduction for delirium in hospitalized older patients compared with standard care.
index-c58-044.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-045.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-045.auditText: Proactive geriatric consultation has been demonstrated to reduce the risk of delirium post hip fracture by 40% in a randomized controlled trial.
index-c58-045.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-046.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-046.auditText: Physical restraints should be avoided in delirious patients because they lead to decreased mobility, increased agitation, and greater risk of injury and worsening delirium.
index-c58-046.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-047.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-047.auditText: The nonpharmacologic sleep protocol includes a glass of warm milk or herbal tea, relaxation music or tapes, and back massage.
index-c58-047.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-048.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-048.auditText: The nonpharmacologic sleep protocol reduced the use of sleeping medications from 54% to 31% in a hospital environment.
index-c58-048.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-058.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-058.auditText: Benzodiazepines are not recommended as first-line agents in the treatment of delirium because of their propensity to cause oversedation and exacerbate acute mental status changes.
index-c58-058.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-059.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-059.auditText: Benzodiazepines remain the treatment of choice for delirium caused by seizures and alcohol- and medication-related withdrawal syndromes.
index-c58-059.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c58-061.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium
index-c58-061.auditText: Of those admitted to postacute care with delirium, over 50% are still delirious 1 month later.
index-c58-061.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-005.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-005.auditText: Late-life onset of neuropsychiatric symptoms of any severity in individuals without dementia, lasting for over 6 months, that are not attributable to another concurrent psychiatric disorder are referred to as mild behavioral impairment (MBI).
index-c60-005.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-006.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-006.auditText: Neuropsychiatric symptoms are seen in up to 98% of patients with dementia.
index-c60-006.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-013.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-013.auditText: The Neuropsychiatric Inventory-Questionnaire (NPI-Q) is a self-administered informant-based instrument that measures the presence and severity of 12 neuropsychiatric symptoms, as well as informant distress.
index-c60-013.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-014.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-014.auditText: Anticholinergics, amantadine, dopaminergic agents, and catechol-O-methyl transferase (COMT) inhibitors can exacerbate psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations and delusions.
index-c60-014.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-020.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-020.auditText: Up to 50% of individuals with dementia will suffer from depression over the course of their illness.
index-c60-020.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-021.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-021.auditText: Psychotic symptoms, such as delusions and hallucinations, occur in 20% to 30% of patients with Alzheimer disease.
index-c60-021.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-022.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-022.auditText: Psychotic symptoms occur in over 50% of patients with dementia with Lewy bodies or Parkinson disease dementia.
index-c60-022.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-023.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-023.auditText: Delusions are more common than hallucinations in dementia.
index-c60-023.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-024.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-024.auditText: In Alzheimer disease, hallucinations are more likely to be visual than auditory, and tend to occur in the moderate to severe stages of dementia.
index-c60-024.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-025.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-025.auditText: Visual hallucinations are more common in dementia with Lewy bodies than Alzheimer disease and may be the most clinically useful feature to distinguish the two.
index-c60-025.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-026.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-026.auditText: The Alzheimer’s Association estimates that 60% to 70% of older adults with Alzheimer disease and other dementias live in the community and are cared for by family and friends.
index-c60-026.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-027.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-027.auditText: The Maximizing Independence at Home (MIND at Home) Study found that 99% of patients with dementia had unmet needs.
index-c60-027.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-029.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-029.auditText: Nonpharmacologic interventions are first-line in the management of neuropsychiatric symptoms in dementia patients to avoid the risks and side effects associated with medications.
index-c60-029.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-032.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-032.auditText: The American Psychiatric Association recommends that if there is no significant response to antipsychotics after a 4-week period, the medication should be tapered and withdrawn.
index-c60-032.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-033.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-033.auditText: In patients whose antipsychotic medications are being tapered, symptoms should be assessed at least every month during tapering and for at least 4 months after the medication is discontinued.
index-c60-033.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-034.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-034.auditText: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics should not be used in patients with dementia unless administered for a co-occurring chronic psychotic disorder.
index-c60-034.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-035.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-035.auditText: Typical antipsychotics, such as haloperidol, should not be used as a first-line neuroleptic in nonemergent situations due to the elevated risk of extrapyramidal side effects.
index-c60-035.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-037.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-037.auditText: Up to 50% of community dwelling older adults with dementia in the United States are prescribed antidepressants.
index-c60-037.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-038.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-038.auditText: Some selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, such as paroxetine, have anticholinergic properties and should be avoided in older adults.
index-c60-038.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-040.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-040.auditText: Valproate, when used solely for organic brain disorders, is ineffective for treating agitation in people with dementia.
index-c60-040.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-041.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-041.auditText: Cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine should not be considered first-line pharmacologic agents in the management of acute neuropsychiatric symptoms of moderate or greater severity.
index-c60-041.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-043.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-043.auditText: Benzodiazepines are used in 8.5% to 20% of patients with Alzheimer disease.
index-c60-043.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c60-046.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 60, BPSD and psychoactive drugs
index-c60-046.auditText: Dextromethorphan-quinidine was approved by the US FDA in 2010 for the treatment of pseudobulbar affect.
index-c60-046.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-001.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-001.auditText: Parkinsonism can be defined as a variable combination of six specific, independent motor features: bradykinesia, tremor at rest, rigidity, loss of postural reflexes, flexed posture, and freezing of gait.
index-c61-001.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-002.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-002.auditText: Idiopathic Parkinson disease is estimated to affect approximately 1% to 2% of people older than age 60.
index-c61-002.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-005.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-005.auditText: Longitudinal clinical postmortem studies suggest that 10% to 20% of patients thought to have Parkinson disease in life will have alternative diagnoses on autopsy.
index-c61-005.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-006.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-006.auditText: Midbrain Lewy bodies are seen on autopsy in about 20% of older individuals without a known history of parkinsonism.
index-c61-006.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-010.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-010.auditText: Parkinson disease is about 1.5 times more common in men than in women.
index-c61-010.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-011.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-011.auditText: Over 90% of cases of Parkinson disease are considered sporadic.
index-c61-011.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-015.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-015.auditText: By the time motor symptoms of Parkinson disease are present, the posterior putamen has undergone profound denervation equating to the loss of over 60% to 80% of dopaminergic terminals.
index-c61-015.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-017.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-017.auditText: Lewy body deposition in the original Braak stage 3 involves the nigra and is thought to correspond with the onset of motor features of Parkinson disease.
index-c61-017.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-018.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-018.auditText: Unlike Parkinson disease, both progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal syndrome are not thought to be disorders of α-synuclein but instead are attributable to misfolded tau.
index-c61-018.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-019.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-019.auditText: Multiple system atrophy is characterized by the development of argyrophilic cytoplasmic inclusion bodies that are positive for α-synuclein in glial cells rather than typical neuronal Lewy bodies.
index-c61-019.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-021.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-021.auditText: A symmetrical onset of symptoms is a helpful clue that one is likely dealing with an alternative cause of parkinsonism other than idiopathic Parkinson disease.
index-c61-021.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-023.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-023.auditText: The tremor caused by Parkinson disease is a predominant rest tremor, whereas essential tremor is not typically present at rest.
index-c61-023.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-024.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-024.auditText: Dopamine transporter single-photon emission computed tomography imaging has been approved to distinguish essential tremor from Parkinson disease in patients with atypical tremor manifestation.
index-c61-024.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-025.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-025.auditText: Individuals meet the threshold for probable dementia with Lewy bodies if they show findings of a progressive dementia and have at least two of four core features.
index-c61-025.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-027.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-027.auditText: About 50% of individuals with Parkinson disease will develop dementia within 10 years of their initial diagnosis.
index-c61-027.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-028.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-028.auditText: The median age of onset for multiple system atrophy is in the sixth decade of life with a mean time to severe disability of approximately 5 years from the time of diagnosis.
index-c61-028.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-029.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-029.auditText: Unlike other atypical parkinsonian conditions, cognitive impairment is not a typical feature of multiple system atrophy.
index-c61-029.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-030.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-030.auditText: Corticobasal syndrome is one of the exceptions to the general rule that asymmetric limb motor involvement favors a diagnosis of Parkinson disease.
index-c61-030.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-031.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-031.auditText: Over half of patients develop troublesome complications of disabling response fluctuations or dyskinesias after 5 years of levodopa therapy.
index-c61-031.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-032.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-032.auditText: Dopamine agonists are more likely than levodopa to cause hallucinations, confusion, and psychosis, especially in older adults.
index-c61-032.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-033.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-033.auditText: It is safer to utilize levodopa than dopamine agonists in patients older than 70 years.
index-c61-033.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-038.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-038.auditText: Adjunctive treatment for drug-induced hallucinations can begin with the addition of quetiapine, starting with 25 mg at bedtime.
index-c61-038.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-041.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-041.auditText: Antimuscarinic drugs should be avoided in patients older than 70 years due to the risk of cognitive impairment and hallucinations.
index-c61-041.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-044.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-044.auditText: Periodic leg movements of sleep and restless legs syndrome are estimated to be twice as common in Parkinson disease as in matched populations.
index-c61-044.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-046.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-046.auditText: Patients with significant speech, gait, depression with suicidal ideation, or cognitive difficulties are usually not good candidates for deep brain stimulation.
index-c61-046.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c61-047.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 61, Parkinson disease and related disorders
index-c61-047.auditText: Deep brain stimulation is not suggested for patients with atypical parkinsonian conditions since the majority of these motor features do not respond to dopaminergic medications.
index-c61-047.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-001.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-001.auditText: Alzheimer disease (AD) is the most common neurodegenerative disorder encountered by the practicing geriatrician.
index-c63-001.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-003.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-003.auditText: The dominance of behavioral and personality changes in the absence of memory and perceptual symptoms is highly suggestive of the behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia (FTD).
index-c63-003.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-004.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-004.auditText: History of falls and dysphagia with abnormalities in vertical gaze and preserved oculocephalic reflex is suggestive of a diagnosis of progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP).
index-c63-004.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-006.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-006.auditText: Recent research criteria for bvFTD require three of six specific symptoms to meet possible criteria.
index-c63-006.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-007.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-007.auditText: Abnormalities in vertical gaze with a preserved oculocephalic reflex are a characteristic finding in progressive supranuclear palsy.
index-c63-007.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-009.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-009.auditText: The reported mean onset of dementia with Lewy bodies is 75 years with a range from 50 to 80 years.
index-c63-009.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-010.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-010.auditText: Dementia with Lewy bodies typically involves better performance on episodic memory tasks and recognition memory when compared to Alzheimer disease patients.
index-c63-010.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-012.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-012.auditText: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder occurs in 85% of dementia with Lewy bodies cases.
index-c63-012.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-013.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-013.auditText: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder occurs in 15% of Parkinson disease patients.
index-c63-013.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-014.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-014.auditText: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder occurs in 60% of patients with multiple system atrophy.
index-c63-014.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-015.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-015.auditText: When rapid eye movement sleep behavior occurs in association with severe autonomic symptoms, multiple system atrophy rather than dementia with Lewy bodies should be considered.
index-c63-015.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-016.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-016.auditText: Significant depressive symptoms occur in up to 40% of dementia with Lewy bodies cases.
index-c63-016.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-018.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-018.auditText: Spontaneous parkinsonism eventually occurs in up to 70% of dementia with Lewy bodies cases.
index-c63-018.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-019.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-019.auditText: In contrast to Parkinson disease, the parkinsonism of dementia with Lewy bodies is more commonly bilateral and less frequently includes tremor.
index-c63-019.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-022.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-022.auditText: Relative sparing of the posterior cingulate cortical perfusion in dementia with Lewy bodies compared to the occipital cortex is a highly specific finding called the cingulate island sign.
index-c63-022.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-025.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-025.auditText: Patients with dementia with Lewy bodies should be advised to avoid anticholinergic medications.
index-c63-025.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-027.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-027.auditText: Death in multiple system atrophy typically occurs within 6 to 10 years.
index-c63-027.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-029.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-029.auditText: The mean age of onset for multiple system atrophy is 54.
index-c63-029.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-032.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-032.auditText: Occurrence of symptoms suggestive of multiple system atrophy in an individual younger than 30 years should raise suspicion for alternative diagnoses.
index-c63-032.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-033.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-033.auditText: About one-third of multiple system atrophy patients respond to levodopa in the early stages of the disease.
index-c63-033.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-034.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-034.auditText: In most centers, behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia accounts for more than 50% of all frontotemporal lobar degeneration cases.
index-c63-034.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-037.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-037.auditText: In contrast to patients with semantic variant primary progressive aphasia, patients with nonfluent variant primary progressive aphasia maintain single word comprehension and semantic knowledge.
index-c63-037.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-038.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-038.auditText: Approximately 20% of patients with nonfluent variant primary progressive aphasia show TDP pathology.
index-c63-038.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-039.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-039.auditText: In contrast to Alzheimer disease, many semantic variant primary progressive aphasia patients have greater deficits for remote compared to recent memory.
index-c63-039.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-040.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-040.auditText: Patients with semantic variant primary progressive aphasia often have TDP-43 type C–positive, tau-negative inclusions at autopsy.
index-c63-040.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-041.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-041.auditText: The mean age of onset for behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia is in the mid-fifties.
index-c63-041.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-043.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-043.auditText: Executive function tests should not be considered mandatory for a diagnosis of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia.
index-c63-043.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-044.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-044.auditText: Pick disease occurs in approximately 20% of clinical cases presenting with signs and symptoms of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia.
index-c63-044.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-046.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-046.auditText: Pick disease is usually associated with 3Rtau.
index-c63-046.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-047.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-047.auditText: Progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration are associated with 4Rtau.
index-c63-047.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-052.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-052.auditText: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis occurs with an incidence of approximately 1 to 2 per 100,000 patients each year.
index-c63-052.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-053.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-053.auditText: Bulbar symptoms are presenting symptoms in about 25% of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis cases.
index-c63-053.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-055.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-055.auditText: The clinical course of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis has only a 50% survival at 3 years.
index-c63-055.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-056.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-056.auditText: About 15% of patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration develop amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
index-c63-056.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-057.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-057.auditText: About 50% of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis patients develop cognitive and behavioral symptoms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration.
index-c63-057.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-058.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-058.auditText: The mean age of disease onset for corticobasal degeneration is in the mid-sixties.
index-c63-058.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-060.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-060.auditText: Pick bodies are absent in corticobasal degeneration.
index-c63-060.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-064.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-064.auditText: Downward gaze palsy has greater specificity for progressive supranuclear palsy because mild vertical gaze limitation is normal with aging.
index-c63-064.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-065.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-065.auditText: Survival for progressive supranuclear palsy is between 6 and 10 years at the time of diagnosis.
index-c63-065.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-066.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-066.auditText: Genetic analyses are estimated to identify only 40% to 60% of familial spinocerebellar ataxia cases.
index-c63-066.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-067.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-067.auditText: Genetic analyses are estimated to identify less than 25% of sporadic spinocerebellar ataxia cases.
index-c63-067.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-068.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-068.auditText: The prevalence of spinocerebellar ataxias is between 1 and 4 per 100,000.
index-c63-068.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-070.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-070.auditText: The rate of epilepsy in Alzheimer disease ranges from 10% to 22% across studies.
index-c63-070.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-071.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-071.auditText: The risk of development of post-traumatic epilepsy is greater than 50% after a penetrating head injury.
index-c63-071.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-072.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-072.auditText: Severity of head injury is defined by the Glasgow Coma Scale, with 13 to 15 being mild injury.
index-c63-072.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-073.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-073.auditText: Severity of head injury is defined by the Glasgow Coma Scale, with 9 to 12 being moderate injury.
index-c63-073.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-074.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-074.auditText: Severity of head injury is defined by the Glasgow Coma Scale, with less than 9 defined as severe traumatic brain injury.
index-c63-074.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

index-c63-075.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 63, Other neurodegenerative disorders
index-c63-075.auditText: The prevalence of postconcussive syndrome following brain injury ranges from 30% to 80%.
index-c63-075.method: Gemini chapter extraction; Eias reports every NUMBER figure matched the cited or immediately adjacent page, with a fabricated-number positive control. RULE/DEF wording unconfirmed.

read-20260920-c58-drugs.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th edition, chapter 58, Delirium medication paragraph
read-20260920-c58-drugs.auditText:
1. THE WITHHELD DAILY CEILINGS ARE NOT ACTUALLY UNRESOLVED.

You withheld the risperidone and olanzapine daily ceilings pending review of the intended regimen. Chapter 58, PDF page 1935, states them in plain prose: an atypical antipsychotic may be considered at a low starting dose — quetiapine starting dose 12.5 mg, 24-hour maximum 25 mg; olanzapine starting dose 2.5 mg, 24-hour maximum 10 mg; or risperidone 0.25 to 0.5 mg, 24-hour maximum 1.5 mg.

Same paragraph, haloperidol: recommended starting dose 0.25 mg orally or parenterally, repeatable every 30 minutes after vital signs are rechecked; most antipsychotic-naive older patients should require a total loading dose of no more than 2.5 mg; maintenance of one-half the loading dose in divided doses over the next 24 hours, tapered over the ensuing 48 hours as agitation resolves.

Restore all of these as text-verified against chapter 58 page 1935. Withholding a number the chapter states is the mirror image of asserting one it does not — for a reader sitting an exam a blank costs the same as an error, and this one is not a judgement call.
